original_question: Every irreversible Finsler metric on S^2 has either exactly 2 or infinitely many distinct prime closed geodesics.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the right ambient object (an irreversible Finsler metric), the right manifold (S^2), the right dichotomy (exactly 2 or infinitely many), and the right counted objects (distinct prime closed geodesics). In fact, it is essentially the official statement of Conjecture 2.2.1. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
missing_details: It should be presented explicitly as an open conjecture/research question, not as an established theorem. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
For a fully stand-alone formulation, introduce the metric as a Finsler metric F on the 2-sphere S^2. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

To remove hidden terminology, "prime closed geodesic" should be clarified as a closed geodesic that is not an iterate of a shorter closed geodesic; the surrounding discussion stresses the need to distinguish genuine closed geodesics from repetitions. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

The counting is of distinct prime closed geodesics, not of geometrically distinct unoriented images; the immediately preceding Katok example counts the same equator traversed in opposite directions as the two closed geodesics in the irreversible case. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

For paper-faithful context, the conjecture is posed after the known result that every irreversible Finsler metric on S^2 has at least two distinct prime closed geodesics. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let F be an irreversible Finsler metric on the 2-sphere S^2. Is the total number of distinct prime closed geodesics of F—where "prime" means not an iterate of a shorter closed geodesic—necessarily either exactly 2 or infinite? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets §2.2 of the survey, not a broader neighboring problem. The nearest official formulation is Conjecture 2.2.1, introduced immediately after the discussion of Katok’s example showing that an irreversible Finsler metric on S^2 can have exactly two closed geodesics, and after the Bangert–Long result that at least two distinct prime closed geodesics always exist in this setting. The nearby context after the conjecture gives supporting evidence for bumpy metrics under a transversality hypothesis and then records Conjectures 2.2.2 and 2.2.3 about hyperbolic and elliptic closed geodesics, which explains the intended scope without changing the target statement. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
